questions.stem: Notebook users complain that Spark sessions take minutes to start. The workspace uses a custom pool for small, interactive jobs. What change gives the fastest session start?

options.text: Increase the custom pool's maximum node count
Turn off autoscale on the custom pool
Use the starter pool, whose clusters are kept ready
Move the notebooks into a different workspace

questions.explanation: Starter pools are kept warm by Fabric, so sessions usually start in seconds. Custom pools start their nodes on demand, which takes longer, and changing their size doesn't change that.

questions.stem: Every notebook in a workspace needs the same Python libraries and Spark properties. How do you provide them by default?

options.text: Put the libraries in a lakehouse Files folder
Paste the same %pip install cell at the top of every notebook
Install the libraries on each developer's PC
Attach an environment with those libraries and properties as the workspace's default environment

questions.explanation: An environment holds libraries and Spark settings, and choosing it as the workspace default in the workspace's Spark settings applies it to notebooks and Spark job definitions that don't pick another.

questions.stem: Which three can you set when you create a custom Spark pool for a workspace? Each correct answer is part of the solution.

options.text: The Git branch the pool uses
Autoscale with a minimum and maximum number of nodes

questions.explanation: A custom pool sets its node size, autoscale range and whether executors are allocated dynamically. Cache periods belong to KQL databases and branches to Git integration.

questions.stem: Several notebooks run one after another for the same user and each waits for its own Spark session. Which workspace setting lets them share a session?
questions.explanation: High concurrency mode lets several notebooks share one Spark session, so later notebooks start without waiting for a new session.
